title: Parsing and building `Profile` and `Sequence` gets faster
body:
libnail builds its two record types from raw bytes in `libnail/src/structs`. nail calls them from `nail/src/io` and `search.rs`.

- `Sequence::from_fasta(buf)` (`sequence.rs`) copies the name and the header details into new `String`s. It then pushes every residue into two `Vec`s, `utf8_bytes` and `digital_bytes`, both with a 255 sentinel in front. Each digital byte comes from a lookup in `UTF8_TO_DIGITAL_AMINO`, a `phf::Map<u8, u8>`.
- `Profile::from_p7hmm(buf)` (`p7hmm.rs`) splits the record into lines, checks each line as UTF-8, and parses the floats with `str::parse` through `split_whitespace`. A `ProfileBuilder` collects the values, and its build produces the `Profile`.
- `Profile::from_blosum_62_and_seq(seq)` (`profile.rs`) builds a profile for a sequence query.

nail parses every target and every query at least once, and every profile query twice: once in `build_pipeline` and once for the mmseqs query db (nail-811f24). Each parse lands in a serial step or on the path to one. Rough per-record costs, derived from the `-s` tree on 2,455,940 MGnify targets and 20,795 Pfam profiles at `-t 8` and not measured directly:

| record | step | seconds | per record |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Sequence` | target db write, one thread | ~4.3 | ~1.8 µs, including the writes |
| `Profile` from p7hmm | pipeline build, one thread at `92de7c5` | 3.07 | ~150 µs |

## Proposal

Measure first. A benchmark per constructor, on these inputs, times the parse apart from the build. That shows where the time goes before anything changes. Candidates once it is measured:

- `from_fasta`: a 256-entry table in place of the `phf::Map`, and no `String` for the details when a caller does not need them.
- `from_p7hmm`: a float parser for p7hmm's fixed number format in place of `str::parse`, and no per-line UTF-8 check.
- the `ProfileBuilder` build, if the measurement puts the cost there and not in the parse.

## Open

- Whether a caller that needs only some of a record, such as the target db writer in nail-fc2ac4, gets a narrower constructor or a cheaper full one.
- Any change to these constructors goes in `libnail/CHANGELOG.md`, and one that changes a public field or signature is breaking.
close_reason: Landed in `94eecda`, `9162fd4`, `6df648a`, `fbf5e2c` and `1e1bac3`: `from_fasta` is 7.3 times faster and `from_p7hmm` about 1.5 times, with bit-identical output. The last note has the numbers and the two options left unbuilt.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text:
Measured at `0aae149`, one thread, with a throwaway binary in `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-parse-bench`. It linked libnail and read each input whole into memory before timing. Inputs were `nail-benchmarks/data/pfam.hmm` (20,795 profiles, 3,457,312 positions, mean length 166) and the 2,455,940 MGnify targets in `tmp-claude/2026-10-08-align-fixed-cost/mgy-db/targets.fa`. Each fasta row is the best of two rounds, which were within 1% of each other.

## `Sequence::from_fasta`

| variant | µs per record |
|---|---|
| `from_fasta` as it is | 1.54 |
| `phf` lookup, details not copied | 1.74 |
| 256-entry table, details copied | 0.21 |
| 256-entry table, details not copied | 0.20 |

The `phf::Map` lookup per residue accounts for about 85% of the time. A `[u8; 256]` table built from `UTF8_TO_DIGITAL_AMINO` cuts the time 7.4 times. Copying the details `String` costs about 0.01 µs, so dropping it gains nothing worth a narrower constructor. The `phf` variant without details ran slower than `from_fasta`, and I did not find out why.

## `Profile::from_p7hmm`

| part | ns per position |
|---|---|
| parse, up to `ProfileBuilder::build` | 595 to 635 |
| `ProfileBuilder::build` | 240 to 266 |
| whole `from_p7hmm` | 832 to 865 |

The parse costs about 70% and the build about 30%. Each range spans two runs.

Over all 163.6M float tokens in Pfam, `str::parse::<f32>` took 7.1 ns per token and 8.7 ns with `exp`. A fixed-format parser took 4.0 ns per token, and 5.0 ns with `exp`. It reads `d+.ddddd` as an integer `n`, falls back to `str::parse` when `n >= 2^24`, and returns `n as f32 / 100000.0`. The result matches `str::parse` exactly. Both `n` and 1e5 are exact in f32, and IEEE division rounds correctly, so the quotient is the correctly rounded decimal. Every one of 163,471,026 tokens matched bit for bit, and 145,537 tokens fell back.

A parse that tokenizes model lines as bytes, with no per-line `str::from_utf8`, uses `split` on `is_ascii_whitespace` in place of `split_whitespace`, and calls the fixed-format parser, took 386 ns per position against 635 in the same run. Every Pfam profile it built compared equal (`PartialEq`) to the current one. The other ~390 ns per position, which covers line splitting, insert lines and the builder's `Option`s, has not been broken down. perf is not installed on this machine.

In `build`, `Alphabet::ambiguity_map()` runs once per position. It allocates seven `Vec`s and takes 40 ns per call, about 16% of the build. Hoisting it out of the loop leaves the results unchanged. Most of the rest is likely the `ln` calls, 20 in f64 and 7 in f32 per position, but this is unmeasured. Changing those `ln` calls would change scores.

## `Profile::from_blosum_62_and_seq`

68 µs per sequence over the first 5,000 MGnify targets. That includes `from_fasta` and goes through the same `build`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/302d4408
notes.text:
Final state at `1e1bac3`, one thread, on the inputs from the first note.

| constructor | start (`0aae149`) | now | commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Sequence::from_fasta` | 1.54 µs/record | 0.21 µs/record | `94eecda` |
| `Profile::from_p7hmm` | ~845 ns/position | ~560 ns/position | `9162fd4`, `6df648a`, `fbf5e2c`, `1e1bac3` |

Every change was checked as bit-identical: the fasta output on all 2,455,940 MGnify targets, and the serialized profile plus `entry_transitions` and both emission tables on all 20,795 Pfam profiles.

Not built, with the reasons:

- SIMD for the p7hmm tokenizer and float parser. They take about 45% of `from_p7hmm`. `read_queries` already parses profiles with `par_iter`, and the target db write is parallel (nail-fc2ac4), so the whole Pfam parse is about 0.3 s of wall time at `-t 8`. SIMD would save about 0.1 s and need separate x86_64 and aarch64 code.
- Dropping the `exp` then `ln` round trip between `negexp` in the parser and `build`. libm takes about 25% of `from_p7hmm`. Removing the round trip changes scores in the last bits, and HMMER makes the same round trip. Not measured.
